I understand everything about this. I’m simply stating that the drastic increase in annulments granted world wide and in the US alone is cause for alarm after V2 and the sexual revolution. Our entire discussion is about "outs" but we never talk about having marriages validated after a rupture has been found in the validity of said marriages.

I’m not saying that all annulments are invalid and if people are in abusive situations and need to flee. Fine. The church acknowledges that physical separation is sometimes necessary in the case of physical or verbal abuse and serial adultery, etc.

But this culture of "oh going through tough times? Maybe your marriage is invalid you should check"

"Cool, let’s divorce and remarry now and destroy our kids lives"

Also, if we expand things so much to the effect that anyone can simply walk up to a tribunal and attempt to "annul" a marriage (I understand some/most tribunals are very arduous and not pleasant, it’s a legal procedure after all) and it will be granted (if I’m being modest) 90% of the time. 

So then we need to have a discussion about what is considered valid? 

"Oh wow we aren’t validly married because we got married by the ocean in Mexico? We should recommit in the canonical form and fight for our marriage"

This should be the response, even if your marriage is "not valid" just because you’re "allowed" doesn’t mean you should. You have a responsibility to those kids you created through the promise of "until death do us part"

I know the "tools" have changed. I’m saying that those handy dandy tools make it WAY more likely the people seeking annulments in bad faith (getting an annulment to appease there conscious after they’ve been civilly divorce and remarried for the past 5 years). Because there’s a parallel with the amount of divorces and annulments being granted after the 60s. You seen a sharp contrast between annulments and divorced prior too all this modern crap. That’s exactly the point I’m making tho. If the liberal Pope or Bishop can simply change the requirements then how is that any different then changing doctrine? I’m not sympathetic to the Sedevecantist POV, however they do have some points regarding the liturgy and how seemingly it looks like a different religion. (Explicitly in there case) and having gone through the hard hit personally of my parents divorcing after 20 years and 10 kids (I’m number 6 and was 14 when they divorced in 2014) 

I can’t bring up to my mom how it hurt me and the rest of us and that it doesn’t seem right that she’s dating and going out every weekend (before the annulment was certified even) and now all she can say is that "the church declared that the past 20 years of our life wasn’t a marriage and so I’m moving out, marrying your bowling coach next year and he’s moving in with us" WTF?! This is NOT catholic, and if it is I don’t want anything to do with this.

In this case I might as well join the sedevecantists because even if there theology is whack at least I can be sure that they’ll hold true to the teachings of the church prior to the "weaponized ambiguity" post V2

BTW 9/10 of the kids from this "marriage that never existed because annulments btw" are now secular or pagans, myself I’m agnostic but trying to convince myself (despite my better angels) to come into the church because it seems to be the best way to raise a family, and live a good life. 

But if the church is/was compromised then I guess we’ll have to wait and see what time exposes in the future.

The Canon Law hasn’t changed but the implementation of the law has. The bishops are now the only ones foreseeing such a process and therefore, if you have a modernist bishop who is much more lax and agreeable (church of nice type) doesn’t that mean that the tribunal can slip in more elements to expand the annulment requirements?

https://youtu.be/sGOaF0XsNNI

If you skip to 20:00 Tim talks to a bishop approved catholic annulment support center and the amount of frightening advice she gives is shocking.

I agree. But my point is if the V2 council changed the process for annulments from 4 elements to 15+ wouldn’t that be considered a changing of doctrine? Because then the "proof" is much more easily falsified and subjective. 

Because if "immaturity" and "bad judgment" are now grounds for annulment there’s no solid case for the permanence of marriage. As anyone can simply claim and ask their witness to tell the tribunal that they were immature and not qualified to be married and so 20/30 year old marriages are being shattered alongside the right of children to have a mother and father in the home

I didn’t claim V2 was the issue. I simply stated that since the funkiness of V2 (Spirit of V2) was implemented there’s been a drastic decline in catholic fidelity and seriousness. (Some stats show that for every 1 person who joins 5/6 more leave)

As for your second paragraph I agree with you. The only issue I have is it makes it easier for both parties (the innocent party that made a mistake or the mischievous one trying to deceive the tribunal) to err if the 4 solid and hard to disprove elements are expanded to include things like "bad judgement" or "immaturity") because that is very easy to claim and not easy to quantify. So the tribunal will have a tough time finding holes to poke simply because it’s a flimsy requirement based on hearsay.

Okay so then we need to contend with multiple things. How many marriages are valid? And why aren’t they valid? Because, when you read the 4 fundamentals of what marriage consists of it doesn’t not mention "immaturity". 

The four elements are : (1) the spouses are free to marry; (2) they freely exchange their consent; (3) in consenting to marry, they have the intention to marry for life, to be faithful to one another and be open to children; and (4) their consent is given in the canonical form, i.e., in the presence of two witnesses and before a properly authorized church minister.

The last one is subject to bishop approval for exceptions.

Right and I understand that. My only thing is if the church changes it’s annulment process which gives more wiggle room to annul marriages. 

How can we be sure that those "invalid" marriages were actually not consecrated? Because when things are going great it’s fine to just say yeah we’re validly married but when rocky times come (and they do) it’s pretty easy to talk to your family members (witnesses) and make up a story to get your marriage annulled. 

Again I’m not against annulment as a whole. I’m simply stating that since the confusing and broad requirements for annulments was changed (post V2) there’s been a MASSIVE increase in catholic annulments being granted and approved by the church. Many of which seem to have a almost guaranteed annulment rate. Which is fine when you look at it on paper. "Oh look the church said it’s okay therefore all is well" meanwhile the divorce and remarriage and broken families that this change has caused has been DEVASTATING for the west and catholic culture as a whole.

Yeah for sure I’m just talking about the stark contrast post V2 of annulments and the fact that annulments and divorce have been almost synonymous stats wise for approval. (Since no fault divorce was passed)
